newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE STILL FACES RED LOCUST DANGER--OFFICIALS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE STILL FACES RED LOCUST DANGER--OFFICIALS.

text.p: Some of Zimbabwe's food crop from the new November/April season may be destroyed by remnants of red locust swarms which invaded the country in August but later moved into Botswana, officials said on Wednesday.
The locusts, which moved in from neighbouring Mozambique last month, destroyed around Z$2 million ($187,265) worth of crops in the Matabeleland region which was hardest-hit by the locust swarms.
This was before the Commercial Farmers' Union (CFU) and the state Agricultural Technical and Extension Service (Agritex) embarked on massive aerial sprays, killing large numbers of locusts.
Others were lured west into Botswana by rains.
"The populations left behind are now dispersed and have gone to ground," CFU Matabaleland spokesman Ben Zietsman said.
He added that these locusts were now breeding and a new adult generation would emerge in February.
Zietsman said while little of the crop and vegetation was destroyed in the past month, newly hatched hoppers which were difficult to spray could damage some of the young crop in December.
